title: Review of c03's FCH protocells: vesicles from noise hold their solute 18-24x on seed 7; chi=0 twin falls to 1.16x
summary: Re-ran world.py and world_chi0.py unchanged on fresh seed 7 (128^2, T=800) and measured with c03's contrast.py. Five closed bilayer vesicles nucleate from white noise by t=32 and persist to t=800; their lumens fill with the solute the bilayer makes (gold in the sheet), lumen/outside contrast 18.5-23.6x in every recorded frame (4-6 lumens), against the chi=0 twin 2.35x at t=80 falling to 1.16x. Amphiphile ring rim/core 2.27, rim/outside 29 (25/38 individually membrane-like). One vesicle swallows a bilayer rod at t~450-700 and turns into a multilamellar onion that loses its lumen, so 4 lumens remain at the end.

observations.S: rerun/seed7/sheet.png t=0: white noise over the whole domain; t=32: five rings
observations.I: rerun/seed7/sheet.png t=32-800: the same four round vesicles at fixed positions and sizes
observations.B: rerun/seed7/radial.png: amphiphile ring rim/core 2.27, rim/outside 29, with a solvent lumen inside
observations.W: rerun_contrast.txt: lumen/outside 18.5-23.6x in every frame t=80-800; rerun_chi0_contrast.txt: 2.35 -> 1.16x

controls_run.W: rerun_chi0/seed7 (world_chi0.py, same seed): contrast 2.35x at t=80 decaying to 1.16x by t=800

verdicts.limitation: The solute is passive (osm=0) and decays slowly, so W shows a barrier holding a released solute, not a solute the cell uses. Vesicles are static (no growth, no division) and one became a lumen-less onion after swallowing a rod. I did not re-run the 1.5x resolution arm; the chi=0 twin keeps D the same, so a uniformly lowered-D twin was not tested.
